artworks.title: Allegory of Prudence
artworks.description: Macchietti’s Florentine allegory personifies Prudence — the Latin afterlife of Greek mētis, counsel and cunning. Catalogued with the Oceanid Metis on Commons, the panel stands in for a figure almost never painted in her own right: Zeus’s first wife survives in art chiefly as the virtue that bears her name.

popCulture.title: Theogony (Zeus and Metis)
popCulture.creator: Hesiod
popCulture.description: Hesiod’s Theogony makes Metis Zeus’s first wife and the counsel he swallows — the archaic poem that fixes the Oceanid as Athena’s mother and the king’s internalized wisdom.
